nodes.title: 4. 현장응급처치 알고리즘
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a field-treatment algorithm appendix for Korean EMTs.  
It lays out:  
1. A universal 2-minute primary survey (scene safety, ABCDE, SAMPLE/OPQRST history, DCAP-BTLS rapid trauma scan) with timed re-assessments.  
2. A cardiac-arrest branch: pre-arrival AED preparation, 30:2 CPR, rhythm check every 2 min, shock vs non-shock pathways, high-quality CPR metrics, advanced airway/IV/ETCO₂ monitoring, and reversible-cause search (5 H’s & 5 T’s) with corresponding treatments.

nodes.title: 1. 심정지
nodes.summary: The excerpt is a field-emergency flow-chart appendix for Korean EMS teams. It prescribes the step-by-step cardiac-arrest protocol: prepare the AED en-route, confirm arrest within 10 s, start 30:2 CPR while attaching the defibrillator, check rhythm every 2 min (5 cycles), shock VF/pVT, continue high-quality compressions with advanced airway, ETCO₂ monitoring and IV access, search for reversible causes (5 H & 5 T) and give cause-specific treatment (fluids, ventilation, warming, etc.).

nodes.title: 2. 심정지(소아)
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a field-treatment flowchart for Korean paramedics covering suspected cardiac arrest and traumatic arrest.  
Key points:  
- On every call that could involve cardiac arrest, bring the AED to the scene; while one medic readies the AED, the other begins high-quality CPR (30:2 for 1 or 2 rescuers).  
- Within 10 s confirm consciousness, breathing, pulse; if absent, start compressions, secure IV access, place advanced airway (10 ventilations/min), monitor ETCO₂, and run 2-min (5-cycle) CPR loops while checking rhythm/shockable status.  
- If shockable (VF/pVT), defibrillate; if non-shockable (PEA/asystole), continue CPR and search for reversible causes using the “5 H’s & 5 T’s” mnemonic, giving specific treatments (fluids 20 mL/kg for hypovolaemia/cardiac tamponade, ventilation for hypoxia, warming for hypothermia, etc.).  
- In obvious traumatic arrest, withhold resuscitation if signs of irreversible death are present (rigor, decapitation, brain matter extrusion, decomposition); otherwise perform rapid (<10 min) scene care (spine immobilisation after airway/haemorrhage control, pelvic/long-bone splinting, haemorrhage control) and immediate transport to the nearest surgical facility.

nodes.title: 3. 외상성 심정지
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a field-care flowchart for Korean EMS teams responding to suspected cardiac arrest.  
Key points:

1. Pre-arrival: bring AED ready; on-scene, one member prepares AED while another starts high-quality CPR.  
2. Rapid (<10 s) check for obvious death signs; if absent, continue CPR, secure airway/IV, monitor ETCO₂, apply spinal precautions only after bleeding/airway control.  
3. 2-min CPR cycles with rhythm/pulse checks; treat shockable rhythms (VF/VT) with defibrillation, search and correct reversible causes (5 H’s & 5 T’s).  
4. After ROSC: maintain airway (OPA/NPA cautions), suction, assist ventilation if needed, monitor vitals/ECG/SpO₂ q2 min, transport to nearest appropriate ED; remain vigilant for re-arrest.

nodes.title: 4. 자발순환회복(ROSC) 후 관리
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a Korean-language field-treatment flowchart (appendix section) for suspected cardiac arrest.  
It lists the key actions from scene arrival through transport: ready the AED en-route, begin immediate CPR while the device is prepared, check rhythm, defibrillate if VF/VT, secure the airway (OPA/NPA with listed contraindications), provide oxygen/ventilation, start an IV, and monitor consciousness, vitals, ECG and SpO₂ every 2 min.  
It gives clear thresholds for assisted ventilation (GCS ≤ V, RR < 8, SpO₂ ≤ 90, shallow breathing), specifies transport to the nearest appropriate emergency facility, warns that arrest may recur en-route, and provides quick-reference algorithms for bradycardia (< 50), tachycardia (> 150), PEA and asystole.

nodes.title: 5. 부정맥
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a field-treatment algorithm chart for Korean paramedics.  
It gives the step-by-step sequence when cardiac arrest is suspected: prepare the AED en-route, start immediate CPR while the defibrillator is readied, check rhythm (VF/VT, asystole, PEA), secure airway, give oxygen/ventilation, establish IV access, monitor ECG & vital signs, and then follow the appropriate bradycardia (< 50) or tachycardia (≥ 150) pathway. A parallel column repeats the same logic for pediatric cases, adding pediatric pads, 100-120 compressions min⁻¹, and 12-20 ventilations min⁻¹.

nodes.title: 6. 부정맥(소아)
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a pediatric-and-adult field-resuscitation quick-reference card (Part 4 Appendix).  
It lists step-by-step actions for suspected cardiac arrest: dispatch with AED ready, concurrent CPR while preparing the AED, pediatric pad placement, 100 % oxygen, airway/ventilation/IV/monitoring, and arrhythmia algorithms (bradycardia < 50, tachycardia ≥ 150).  
It then gives the stop-CPR checklist: no response/breath/pulse plus one of—dangerous scene, rescuer exhaustion, “withhold” criteria met, or on-line medical order—while stressing that only a physician can declare death and that resuscitation continues if any doubt exists.  
Special populations (pregnancy, ≤ 18 y, hypothermia, drowning) require medical direction before termination, and extended submersion cases are exempt from the 2-hour rule.

nodes.title: 7. 심정지(소생술 중단 고려)
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a field-treatment flowchart for Korean paramedics who encounter cardiac arrest.  
It lists the sequence: confirm arrest → begin CPR → consider transport → check reversible causes → decide whether to stop CPR.  
It then specifies four acceptable grounds for terminating resuscitation (dangerous scene, rescuer exhaustion, patient meets “CPR-omit” criteria, or on-line medical command orders stop).  
A caution box stresses that only a physician can declare death and that any doubt obliges continued resuscitation.  
Finally, it names absolute exceptions—pregnancy, minors <18, hypothermia, and drowning (unless submersion >2 h)—in which CPR must continue regardless.

nodes.title: 8. 심정지(소생술 유보 고려)
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a field-treatment appendix for Korean EMS personnel.  
It first lists the explicit criteria and mandatory steps for withholding or terminating CPR (obvious death signs, valid DNAR, dangerous scene, mass-casualty triage, required physician consultation, scene preservation, police hand-over, and complete documentation).  

The remainder gives a rapid-assessment and management flow for any patient found in shock or cardiac arrest: check ABCs/LOC/vitals, high-flow O₂, IV access, treat suspected anaphylaxis/sepsis, position for comfort, monitor SpO₂/EKG, keep warm (unless septic), provide fluids, consider airway/ventilatory support, and record all findings and interventions before urgent transport.

nodes.title: 9. 쇼크
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a field-emergency treatment algorithm for Korean EMTs.  
It lists step-by-step actions for undifferentiated shock and airway compromise:

1. Initial survey: check ABCs, level of consciousness, vital signs, give high-flow O₂.  
2. Rapidly identify and treat causes: hypovolemic/traumatic shock, anaphylaxis (stridor, wheeze, facial swelling), sepsis (≥40 °C, meningitic symptoms).  
3. Shock management: secure IV access, elevate legs, fluid challenge, keep SpO₂ ≥95 %, consider intubation/BVM, monitor ECG.  
4. Airway obstruction protocol: assess cough, clear visible foreign bodies, perform back blows / Heimlich, switch to CPR if consciousness lost.  
5. Document findings: vitals, ECG, lung sounds, anaphylaxis trigger, shock signs (pulse >120, SBP <90, skin changes, confusion, etc.).

nodes.title: 10. 기도폐쇄
nodes.summary: The excerpt is a field-first-aid flowchart for airway obstruction and respiratory emergencies. It lists step-by-step actions: check consciousness/remove visible foreign bodies, open airway, encourage coughing or back blows/Heimlich, supply oxygen (nasal 1–5 L, face mask 6–10 L, non-rebreather 11–15 L), monitor SpO₂, and if the patient collapses start CPR immediately. Special notes cover cervical-spine precautions, pregnancy/obesity/infant modifications, suctioning, BVM ventilation, and acceptable SpO₂ 85–90 % for COPD patients.

nodes.title: 11. 기도유지
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a field-protocol appendix that summarizes, in bullet-note form, the key steps for assessing and managing a patient’s airway and breathing in an emergency.  
Main points covered:  
- Rapid respiratory assessment (look-listen-feel, SpO₂, ETCO₂, EKG, vital signs, LOC).  
- Cervical-spine precautions while opening the airway.  
- Suction timing/technique (≤15 s, in-and-out motion) and airway-cleaning checks.  
- Oxygen-delivery options by device and flow rate (nasal cannula 1–5 L, simple face mask 6–10 L, non-rebreather 11–15 L).  
- Acceptable SpO₂ target 85–90 % for COPD patients with home O₂.  
- When to consider BVM ventilation and/or intubation (age-appropriate equipment).  
- Step-by-step newborn/infant airway management including oro/nasal suction, pre-ventilation, and confirmation of airway clearance before proceeding.

nodes.title: 12. 흡인
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a field-emergency-treatment algorithm for paramedics.  
It gives step-by-step rules for:

- Newborn & adult airway management (positioning, suctioning, BVM ventilation, ET-tube/trach considerations)  
- Rapid patient assessment (consciousness, breathing, pulse, SpO₂, blood pressure, ECG)  
- Oxygen delivery choices (nasal cannula, face mask, NRB) and bronchodilator use, with special notes for COPD and respiratory disease patients  
- Transport decisions: when to call on-line medical direction, which patients need a tertiary emergency center, and when to escalate to definitive airway or advanced care.

nodes.title: 13. 호흡곤란
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a two-page flow-chart appendix for field EMS crews on how to rapidly assess and manage a dyspnoeic or altered-consciousness patient.  
Key points covered:

1. Initial “ABCs” check: consciousness → breathing pattern/rate → pulse → cardiac arrest algorithm.  
2. Immediate airway/ventilation actions: 100 % O₂ via BVM 15 L/min (12–20 breaths/min) if abnormal breathing or SpO₂ < 94 %.  
3. Targeted physical exam items: cyanosis, JVD, chest shape, pitting edema, blood pressure cut-offs (≤90 or ≥200), tachycardia/bradycardia significance.  
4. Oxygen-delivery rules: nasal cannula 1–5 L/min, simple face mask 6–10 L/min, non-rebreather 11–15 L/min; special step-wise O₂ for COPD.  
5. Differential cues to distinguish upper-airway obstruction, asthma/COPD, acute heart failure, anaphylaxis.  
6. Transport decision: severe distress, low SpO₂, or need for advanced airway/bronchodilator → direct to regional emergency medical center; otherwise local ER.

nodes.title: 14. 호흡곤란(소아)
nodes.summary: The excerpt is a field-treatment flowchart for Korean paramedics. It gives step-by-step criteria to assess a patient’s consciousness and breathing (“ABCs”), decide if the pattern is normal or abnormal, and immediately intervene: open airway, BVM ventilation with 100 % O₂, or simple face-mask O₂. It lists red-flag signs (low SpO₂, paradoxical breathing, severe retractions, bradypnea by age) and branching pathways for asthma, COPD, acute heart failure, anaphylaxis, or foreign-body airway obstruction. Finally it instructs how to calm and coach slow breathing for hyperventilation, document vitals/ECG/SpO₂, and choose the nearest appropriate ED versus a tertiary emergency center when critical causes (MI, PE, etc.) are suspected.

nodes.title: 15. 과호흡
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a field-triage flowchart and treatment checklist for two Korean EMS scenarios:  
1. Hyperventilation – rapid assessment of ABCs/V/S/SpO₂, rule-out critical causes, coach slow breathing with face-mask O₂ 6–10 L/min, document triggers/history, forbid bag-mask except self-administration.  
2. Suspected acute cardiac chest pain – immediate O₂ to keep SpO₂ ≥94%, 12-lead ECG for ST-elevation MI, NTG protocol (3 doses, 3–5 min apart) with strict contraindications, IV access, transmit ECG, destination criteria (regional EMS center vs. reperfusion-capable hospital), full documentation of vitals, findings, and history.

nodes.title: 16. 흉통
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a field-treatment protocol for Korean EMT-paramedics dealing with acute chest-pain/respiratory-distress patients.  
Main points:  
1. Primary survey sequence – ABCs, vitals, SpO₂; lung auscultation; calm/reassure patient; OPQRST history.  
2. Oxygen titration to keep SpO₂ ≥ 94 %.  
3. 12-lead ECG acquisition, rapid interpretation for STEMI, immediate transmission to receiving hospital.  
4. Nitroglycerin (NTG) administration rules: up to 3 SL doses 3–5 min apart, strict contraindications (SBP ≤ 90 mmHg, severe bradycardia/tachycardia, recent PDE-5 inhibitors, glaucoma, CNS bleeding, suspected RV infarct); post-NTG hypotension → 500 mL NS bolus.  
5. IV access (18 G, NS) and patient-supplied NTG use.  
6. Destination decisions: chest-pain → regional ED; STEMI → PCI-capable facility; unstable or remote area → shortest transport or on-line medical direction.  
7. Documentation checklist – ABCs, ECG, SpO₂, EtCO₂, symptoms, history, lung sounds, skin colour/diaphoresis.  
8. STEMI localisation patterns on ECG (anterior, inferior, lateral, posterior).  
9. Additional flow-chart for SpO₂ ≤ 94 % or hypotension: escalate oxygen (nasal → face-mask → NRB), consider advanced airway, elevate legs, early IV fluid (300 mL NS/LR adult, 5 mL/kg paediatric) if transport > 20 min.  
10. Haemoptysis module – assess volume, colour/foam, associated symptoms, relevant history (lung disease, anticoagulants, recent procedures); large or shock → regional ED; hand over any expectorated blood.

nodes.title: 17. 객혈
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a Korean-language emergency-care flowchart (appendix section) that gives step-by-step field protocols for two scenarios: (1) hemoptysis and (2) hematemesis/melena.  
Main points:

- Triage decision tree based on SpO₂ ≤ 94 % and systolic BP ≤ 90 mmHg.  
- Immediate actions: airway management, oxygen delivery algorithms (nasal cannula 1–5 L/min → simple mask 6–10 L/min → non-rebreather 11–15 L/min), leg elevation, IV access with crystalloid dosing (adult 300 mL NS/RL, pediatric 5 mL/kg) if transport >20 min.  
- Consider advanced airway before transport; continuous monitoring of ABCs, vitals, SpO₂, ECG.  
- Transport destination rules: patients with respiratory failure, shock, or massive bleeding (>150 mL/h) must go to a regional emergency medical center or higher.  
- Mandatory documentation: initial assessments, history (pulmonary/GI disease, anticoagulants, recent procedures), associated symptoms, bleeding characteristics (color, foam, food particles, bright-red foam in sputum), and physical findings (jaundice, ascites, angiomata, dependent edema).  
- Emphasis on handing over any expectorated or vomited blood to the receiving hospital and noting infection risk to crew.

nodes.title: 18. 토혈/혈변
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a field-triage flowchart and documentation checklist for Korean EMTs treating patients with hematemesis/melena or shock-like states.  
Main points:  
1. Rapid primary survey sequence (ABCs, vitals, SpO₂, BP) with thresholds SpO₂ ≤ 94 % and systolic BP ≤ 90 mmHg triggering oxygen and IV fluid protocols.  
2. Stepwise oxygen delivery (nasal cannula → simple mask → non-rebreather) and shock management (leg elevation, IV 300 mL N/S or LR for adults, 5 mL/kg for pediatrics).  
3. Indications for advanced airway, urgent transport to regional emergency center (especially variceal or shock patients), and continuous monitoring.  
4. Mandatory documentation items: vital trends, GI bleeding characteristics (amount, color, food particles), associated symptoms (fever, chest/abdominal pain), stigmata of liver disease, and any witnessed hematemesis/melena on scene.

nodes.title: 19. 구토/설사
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a Korean-language field-triage appendix that gives step-by-step emergency care algorithms for two chief complaints:  
1) Suspected GI bleeding/vomiting-diarrhoea with possible shock  
2) Acute abdominal pain  

For each it lists:  
- Primary & secondary assessment sequence (ABCs, vitals, LOC, SpO₂, BP)  
- Immediate interventions: positioning (lateral recumbent if vomiting, shock position), NPO, warming, airway/oxygen (nasal cannula 1–5 L → face mask 6–10 L → non-rebreather 11–15 L), IV access & fluid, monitoring, rapid transport criteria (SpO₂ ≤ 94 % or systolic BP ≤ 90 mmHg)  
- Focused abdominal exam order (inspection → auscultation → percussion → palpation) and ECG consideration  
- Key documentation points: symptom onset, amount/frequency of vomitus/stool, presence of blood, abdominal distension/rigidity, pain score/pattern/radiation, associated symptoms (nausea, bowel sounds, rebound), relevant history (food intake, cardiac history, medications, last menses/pregnancy, prior similar episodes, prostate disease)  
- Special notes: elderly may present abdominal pain from ischemic cardiac pain or BPH

nodes.title: 20. 복통
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a field-treatment protocol card for Korean EMTs.  
It gives a step-by-step algorithm for two situations:

1. Adult acute abdomen / chest pain  
   - Rapid primary survey (ABCs, vitals, SpO₂)  
   - Oxygen titration, IV access, shock position, NPO  
   - Focused secondary survey: pain history, abdominal inspection–auscultation–palpation, ECG, pregnancy check, documentation points

2. Emergency childbirth / newborn care  
   - Maternal bleeding control (pads, uterine massage)  
   - Delivery sequence: left-lateral, suction, shoulder delivery, placental delivery, post-partum hemorrhage check  
   - Newborn airway, drying, cord care, respiration assessment, separate records, hospital pre-alert

nodes.title: 21. 분만
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a Korean-language field-emergency flowchart (appendix) for paramedics.  
It gives rapid yes/no checkpoints and step-by-step actions for:

- Emergency childbirth on-scene: checking for bleeding, shock, visible presenting parts, rupture of membranes, shoulder delivery, placental delivery, newborn airway clearance, cord care, thermal protection, and immediate neonatal resuscitation.  
- Maternal post-partum care: fundal massage for hemorrhage, transport criteria, twin-birth alert.  
- General critical-care protocol: primary survey (ABCs), oxygen delivery routes, vital-sign thresholds (BP ≥90 mmHg, SpO₂ ≤94 %, temp ≥38 °C, BGL <70 mg/dL), algorithms for hypoglycaemia, hyperthermia, toxidromes (scopolamine, glutethimide, narcotics), plus indications for advanced airway, IV access, fluid/glucose bolus, ECG, and direct medical consultation.

nodes.title: 22. 의식저하
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a field-treatment flowchart for Korean paramedics. It gives step-by-step algorithms for the first 10–15 minutes of an unconscious or altered-consciousness call:  
1. Rapid “ABCs” & vital-sign survey (BP, SpO₂, temp, glucose, pupils).  
2. Immediate actions: high-flow O₂, ECG, leg-raise, IV access.  
3. Branching pathways for hypoglycaemia (glucose ≤70 mg/dL), hyperthermia, shock (BP ≤90), suspected toxin or stroke.  
4. Red-flag criteria that force on-line medical direction or direct transport to a regional emergency center.  
5. Mandatory documentation points: GCS, symptom onset time, last known normal, response to dextrose, scene clues (needle marks, breath odor, trauma).

nodes.title: 23. 저혈당
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a Korean-language field-protocol appendix for pre-hospital emergency care.  
It presents rapid-response algorithms for three critical situations—shock, hypoglycaemia, and suspected stroke—each triggered by threshold vital-sign checks (blood pressure ≤ 90 mmHg, glucose ≤ 70 mg/dL, new-onset stroke signs within 6 h).  
For every scenario it lists the sequence of ABC/VS/LOC assessment, oxygen delivery, airway management, IV access, glucose or fluid administration, ECG monitoring, and mandatory documentation (GCS, SpO₂, blood sugar, event times, patient history).  
Additional notes cover abnormal respiratory patterns, transport decisions to designated stroke-capable centres, and safety precautions such as never leaving the patient unattended and preparing for aggressive behaviour.

nodes.title: 24. 뇌졸중
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a field-protocol cheat-sheet for Korean EMTs covering two chief complaints:

1. Suspected stroke  
   - Rapid scene assessment (onset time, LNT/FAT, Cincinnati Prehospital Stroke Scale: facial droop, arm drift, speech).  
   - Immediate care: airway/oxygen if SpO₂ ≤ 94, glucose if < 70 mg/dL, blood-pressure positioning (head-up vs. Trendelenburg), ECG monitoring.  
   - Destination rule: patients within 6 h of onset and positive screen go to a thrombolysis-capable regional stroke center.

2. Seizure  
   - Scene safety and patient protection (remove glasses, pad head, lateral recumbent if no trauma).  
   - Never force mouth open or give PO meds.  
   - Monitor ABCs, vitals, SpO₂, ECG; suction as needed.  
   - Transport choice: ongoing seizure → nearest ER; resolved seizure → regional emergency center; pregnant → nearest OB-capable facility.  
   - Hand-over data: seizure duration, frequency, witnessed behavior, incontinence, tongue injury, meds/alcohol, temperature, glucose.

Both sections embed flow-chart style yes/no checks for hypoglycaemia and hypoxia.

nodes.title: 25. 발작/경련
nodes.summary: The excerpt is a Korean-language emergency-medicine appendix that lists step-by-step field seizure-management protocols for EMS personnel: initial assessment (ABCs, vitals, SpO₂), airway protection, patient safety positioning, oxygen delivery, suctioning, prohibition of forced oral insertion, monitoring (ECG, LOC), dextrose administration for hypoglycaemia, high-flow oxygen or assisted ventilation if cyanosis/SpO₂ < 90 % persists, post-seizure re-evaluation, and rapid transport rules (active seizure → nearest ER, resolved seizure → regional emergency centre, pregnant woman → obstetric-capable facility). It also specifies documentation items: seizure history, duration, frequency, incontinence, oral injury, temperature, drugs/alcohol, and vitals.

nodes.title: 26. 발작/경련(소아)
nodes.summary: The excerpt is a Korean pre-hospital emergency-care protocol for seizure/hypoglycaemia management by paramedics. Key elements: rapid ABC & vital-sign assessment, high-flow O₂, suction, protect patient, left-lateral position, no forced airway insertion. Detailed hypoglycaemia algorithm—check blood glucose, give oral 50 % glucose (child 50 ml, adult 100 ml) if alert; otherwise start IV 10 % glucose (5 ml kg⁻¹). Re-check glucose q 30-60 min; if vomiting, prevent aspiration. After treatment, if conscious and improved transport to local ED; if still unconscious or other causes suspected, go to regional emergency centre. Continuously monitor ABCs, vitals, ECG, seizure course; document seizure history, duration, incontinence, oral injury, temperature, meds and treatments given.

nodes.title: 27. 저혈당(의식있음)
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a field-treatment flowchart (appendix section) for emergency-medical-service crews.  
It gives step-by-step protocols for two chief complaints:

1. Hypoglycaemia  
   – Rapid oral glucose (50 % dextrose 50 mL / 100 mL by age) while keeping the patient semi-recumbent.  
   – Re-check blood glucose q 30–60 min; if vomiting, protect airway from aspiration.  
   – If no rapid improvement or altered consciousness persists, escalate to IV glucose (10 % or 50 % dextrose by age) and transport to higher-level emergency facility; document insulin use, dialysis, response to glucose, and rule-out stroke, head trauma, seizure, other metabolic causes.

2. Febrile illness with suspected sepsis / meningitis (especially after overseas travel)  
   – Assess ABCs, vitals, mental status, travel history.  
   – Red-flag criteria: temp ≥ 40 °C, severe systemic symptoms, lymphadenopathy, meningeal signs, SpO₂ ≤ 95 %, hypotension, organ-failure signs.  
   – Put on PPE, start cooling (lukewarm massage, ice packs), give oxygen (nasal cannula 1–5 L/min or face mask 6–10 L/min; non-rebreather 11–15 L/min if needed), establish IV access and fluid bolus (300 mL → 1 L if shock persists).  
   – Notify public-health office if travel within 3 weeks; transport to appropriate emergency level based on severity.

nodes.title: 28. 고열/열사병
nodes.summary: The excerpt is a field-treatment flowchart for Korean EMTs. It gives step-by-step emergency protocols for three situations: (1) suspected severe infection/sepsis after overseas travel—highlighting ABCs, high fever, meningeal signs, oxygen, cooling, fluid resuscitation and transfer; (2) newborn resuscitation—covering APGAR scoring, breathing assistance (BVM 40–60/min), chest compressions 3:1, oxygen, IV access, and possible causes such as prematurity, hypoglycaemia, hypothermia; (3) obstetric bleeding—emphasising ABCs/LOC, no vaginal exam, shock position, uterine massage, large-bore IV fluids, left-lateral position, warming, urgent transfer, and documenting estimated blood loss, tissue passed, LMP and pregnancy status.

nodes.title: 29. 임신부 출산
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a field-emergency protocol card for Korean EMTs.  
It lists step-by-step on-scene actions: rapid primary survey (ABCs, vitals, GCS), control of airway/oxygen, hemorrhage control (direct pressure, dressings, tourniquet), fracture immobilization (pelvic binder, long-bone traction splints), spinal motion restriction, and shock management (positioning, warming, IV fluid goals 70–80 mmHg for bleeding without head injury, 110–160 mmHg with head injury).  
Special notes cover pregnancy-related bleeding, privacy, minimal scene time (<10 min), and high-risk conditions (tension pneumothorax, cardiac tamponade, open chest wound, etc.).

nodes.title: 30. 다발성 외상
nodes.summary:
The partial document is a Korean-language field-triage appendix that presents rapid on-scene trauma care algorithms. Core points:  
1. Scene-time target <10 min; immediate GCS assessment and airway-breathing-circulation focus.  
2. Early airway control maneuvers (OPA/NPA selection based on gag reflex, cervical-spine precautions).  
3. Hemorrhage control sequence: wound cleaning → pressure dressing → tourniquet if needed; maintain SBP 70–80 mmHg for non-head bleeding, 110–160 mmHg for head-injured bleeding.  
4. Fracture management: pelvic binder, long-bone traction splint, log-roll for all patient moves.  
5. Head-injury pathway: GCS <8 triggers spinal immobilization, 30° head elevation, EtCO₂ 30–35 mmHg, 94–98 % O₂; monitor for herniation signs (fixed pupils, Cushing reflex).  
6. Chest, multisystem and shock algorithms list key injuries to anticipate (tension pneumothorax, cardiac tamponade, open chest wound, hypothermia, etc.).

nodes.title: 31. 머리손상
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a Korean pre-hospital trauma protocol flow-chart for emergency medical technicians.  
It gives step-by-step decision trees for:

1. Head injury / suspected skull-base fracture:  
   – Rapid GCS screen (<8 vs ≥8), repeated every 5 min.  
   – Airway opening manoeuvres (OPA if no gag, NPA if gag present; no manipulation if basal skull fracture suspected).  
   – Oxygen delivery goals (SpO₂ 94–98 %, EtCO₂ 30–35 mmHg).  
   – Control external bleeding with sterile gauze, elevate head 30° if cerebral herniation signs, maintain SBP >110 mmHg with IV fluids.

2. Raised intracranial pressure / brain herniation warning signs:  
   – Fixed/dilated pupils, Cushing reflex, repeated vomiting, abnormal posturing → hyperventilate with 100 % O₂.

3. Detailed GCS scoring table (eye, verbal, motor).

4. Spinal clearance algorithm:  
   – Check age, mechanism, distracting injury, neurological deficit, mid-line tenderness/deformity.  
   – If any positive finding → full spinal immobilisation (cervical collar + head blocks, log-roll only).  
   – Special notes: remove full-face helmet after immobilisation, ensure airway protection if vomiting occurs, never range-of-motion test when tenderness/deformity present.

nodes.title: 32. 척추손상
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a Korean-language field-triage appendix that gives EMTs rapid yes/no checklists and action algorithms for two major trauma scenarios:

1. Suspected spinal injury  
   - Quick screen: age ≤10 or ≥55, altered mental status, neurologic deficit, distracting injury, midline spine pain/deformity/tenderness.  
   - If any criterion is met, immediate spinal motion-restriction (backboard + head blocks; helmet removal protocol for full-face types).  
   - Airway/oxygenation, hypotension (SBP <90 mmHg) and ventilation rules (SpO₂ ≤94 % → nasal/facemask O₂ or BVM) are applied while the patient remains immobilised.  
   - Special notes: log-roll only after life-threatening bleeding is controlled, no range-of-motion testing if tenderness/deformity present, cervical collar alone is insufficient, aspiration precautions if vomiting occurs.

2. Penetrating chest trauma  
   - Primary survey (CAB) with concurrent life-saving interventions: open pneumothorax → 3-sided dressing; massive external bleeding → direct pressure; impaled object → stabilise, do not remove.  
   - All chest stab wounds mandate consideration of intra-abdominal/retroperitoneal bleeding; prepare for intubation and positive-pressure ventilation.  
   - Monitor SpO₂, ECG; keep on-scene time <10 min.  
   - Associated findings to remember: upper rib fractures suggest high-energy injury (major vessels, head trauma); lower rib fractures raise suspicion of solid-organ abdominal injury.

nodes.title: 33. 흉부 관통상
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a field-treatment protocol for Korean EMTs covering penetrating chest/abdominal/pelvic trauma.  
Key points: rapid (<10 min) scene management; C-A-B assessment with airway maneuvers (OPA/NPA), oxygen/BVM for SpO₂ ≤94%, IV crystalloid if SBP <90 mmHg; specific actions for open pneumothorax (3-sided dressing), external bleeding (sterile gauze pressure), impaled objects (stabilize, do not remove), flail chest/pelvic fractures (binders), evisceration (saline-moistened dressing); emphasis on occult intra-thoracic/intra-abdominal bleeding, continuous monitoring (SpO₂, ECG), and early transport.

nodes.title: 34. 복부 외상
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a field-triage “cheat-sheet” for Korean EMS crews.  
It lists the 4-part primary survey (C-A-B) and gives step-by-step, time-critical interventions for:

- Penetrating abdominal wounds (sterile gauze pressure, exposed bowel dressing, impaled object left in place).  
- Suspected pelvic fracture (pelvic binder, shock watch).  
- Airway/oxygenation (OPA vs NPA choice, SpO₂ ≤ 94 % → nasal cannula / face mask / BVM).  
- Hypotension (IV 18 G, normal saline, rapid transport < 10 min).  

A second flowchart covers multisystem trauma: control bleeding (pack, pressure, tourniquet), splint long-bone and joint injuries (check neurovascular status before/after), manage amputations (rinse, wrap in saline gauze, cool but don’t freeze), and reminds crews to monitor/reassess vitals en-route and keep on-scene time under 10 min.

nodes.title: 35. 골절 및 절단
nodes.summary: The excerpt is a field-treatment algorithm for emergency-medical technicians dealing with polytrauma, severe bleeding, fractures/dislocations, amputations, and eye injuries. It lists step-by-step on-scene actions: control hemorrhage with dressings/tourniquets, splint long bones while monitoring neurovascular status, preserve amputated parts (clean, moisten with saline, cool in sealed bag), and manage ocular trauma—irrigate chemical burns for ≥30 min, shield both eyes, never remove impaled objects, and avoid repositioning a prolapsed globe. Emphasis is placed on completing all trauma care within 10 min for critical patients, continuously assessing ABCs/vitals, and promptly switching to shock guidelines if hypotension appears.

nodes.title: 36. 안구 손상
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a field-triage appendix (Part 4) that gives paramedics step-by-step eye-injury and dental-trauma protocols.  
For eye trauma it stresses: rapid ABC & vital-sign assessment, bilateral eye-shielding, immediate 30-min saline irrigation, strict ban on removing impaled objects or re-positioning a prolapsed globe, and elevation of the head (if no spinal injury) to lower intra-ocular pressure.  
For oral trauma it covers: control of bleeding with gauze, search for avulsed teeth, protect the root surface (minimal saline rinse, keep moist in saline gauze), and triage to a trauma center or dental hospital; if a tooth is missing, assume airway aspiration and do not delay transport to look for it.

nodes.title: 37. 치과적 손상
nodes.summary: The excerpt is a field-emergency-treatment guideline for paramedics. It details the initial trauma assessment (airway-breathing-circulation, vital signs, oral-cavity inspection) and specific measures: pressure dressing for soft-tissue bleeding, management of missing or avulsed teeth (handle only by the crown, store in saline-moistened gauze, avoid delays in transfer), and algorithms for controlling hemorrhage, shock, chest, abdominal and pelvic injuries (e.g., three-sided occlusive dressing for open pneumothorax, pelvic binder, no removal of impaled objects).

nodes.title: 38. 출혈
nodes.summary: The excerpt is a Korean-language field-triage appendix that gives EMTs rapid-reference algorithms and key points for controlling bleeding, managing chest/abdominal/pelvic trauma, and treating burns/chemical injuries. Core content includes: when to apply direct vs. indirect pressure; signs of arterial bleeding, shock, and internal hemorrhage; step-by-step care for open pneumothorax, flail chest, impaled objects, evisceration, and pelvic fractures; standard burn protocols (cooling, dressing, monitoring for airway burns, electrical/chemical exposure); and rules for scene-time <10 min in severe cases.

nodes.title: 39. 화상
nodes.summary:
This section is a field emergency-care protocol for paramedics treating burn and electrical-injury patients.  
Key points:  
- Scene safety and power isolation first.  
- Primary survey: ABCs, airway management (OPA/NPA), 100 % O₂, early advanced airway if needed.  
- Burn care: remove jewelry/clothing, cool contaminated areas with saline or water, separate digits, dry sterile dressing, monitor for arrhythmia.  
- Chemical burns: flush eyes/skin 10–30 min, brush off powders first.  
- Define major burns: ≥5 % 3rd-degree, ≥20 % 2nd-degree, face/hands/genitals/joints, electrical/chemical/inhalation injuries.  
- Electrical/lightning injuries: monitor ECG regardless of voltage, expect entry/exit wounds, deep tissue damage, sudden arrhythmias; spinal immobilize all.  
- Minimize on-scene time to <10 min for severe cases, request burn-center referral, continuous monitoring en route.

nodes.title: 40. 전기 및 낙뢰 손상
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a field-first-aid flowchart appendix for emergency medical technicians.  
It gives step-by-step action cards for three trauma scenarios:  
1. Electrical/lightning injury – scene safety (power isolation), patient removal, ABCs with airway adjunct choice (OPA vs NPA), 100 % O₂, cervical-spine immobilisation, fracture splinting, wound dressing, ECG monitoring for lethal arrhythmias, special notes on entry-exit burns and fern-pattern skin marks.  
2. Suspected head/spine trauma after fall or diving accident – same ABC sequence, airway manoeuvre restrictions if basal skull fracture is possible, SpO₂-guided oxygen delivery, IV access, continuous monitoring, mandatory spinal immobilisation.  
3. Submersion/near-drowning – record immersion time, water temperature, possible seizure, pregnancy; remove wet clothing, prevent hypothermia, oxygen support, monitoring of ABCs, vitals, SpO₂, EtCO₂.  

Throughout, emphasis is placed on crew safety, early ECG and vital-sign monitoring, rapid transport, and priority treatment of arrest victims regardless of usual triage rules.

nodes.title: 41. 익수
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a field-emergency protocol for paramedics treating water-related or diving accidents.  
It presents step-by-step algorithms covering:  
1. Safe patient extraction and spinal-motion restriction when head/spine injury is suspected.  
2. Primary survey (ABCs), airway management (OPA/NPA selection, intubation if needed), oxygen titration by SpO₂, IV access and fluid, ECG monitoring, and temperature control.  
3. Drowning/immersion specifics: document submersion time, activity, water temperature, pregnancy; remove wet clothing, keep warm, assist ventilation.  
4. Neurological checks (orientation, pupils, vision, facial/tongue movement, hearing, motor/sensory function).  
5. Recognition and field care of decompression illness (arterial gas embolism, decompression sickness) with high-flow O₂, consider intubation/IV, and urgent transfer to a hyperbaric-capable facility.

nodes.title: 42. 잠수병
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a field-triage appendix that gives Korean-language emergency-care algorithms for diving-related and cold-exposure illness.  
Core points:  
1. Rapid primary survey – check consciousness, ABCs, vitals; if no pulse/respiration start cardiac arrest protocol.  
2. Suspected arterial gas embolism or decompression sickness – give 100 % O₂, consider intubation/IV access, transport to hyperbaric facility, minimise movement.  
3. Detailed neurological exam checklist (orientation, pupils, vision, facial & limb strength/sensation, hearing, swallowing).  
4. Cold injury management – passive rewarming, remove wet clothes, keep limbs below heart level, avoid rubbing or popping blisters, monitor for hypothermia-induced brady-arrhythmias.  
5. Document exposure circumstances, vital signs, ECG, level of consciousness and clinical grade of hypothermia (mild ≥ 34 °C, moderate 30–34 °C, severe < 30 °C).

nodes.title: 43. 저체온증
nodes.summary:
This section of the Korean EMS field-emergency guideline summarizes pre-hospital care algorithms for hypothermia and hyperthermia.  
Core contents:

- Scene assessment: quick check for apnea/pulse to rule out cardiac arrest; obtain V/S, history, ECG; ensure airway, oxygen (1-15 L/min per device), IV access, warm/cool environment.

- Hypothermia protocol: prevent further heat loss—remove wet clothes, insulate, avoid unnecessary movement, no rubbing or popping blisters, elevate frozen limbs; consider analgesic; watch for bradycardia, arrhythmia from rough handling; document ABCs, V/S, LOC, ECG, exposure time/setting, severity (mild 34°C, moderate 30-34°C, severe <30°C).

- Hyperthermia/heatstroke protocol: move patient to cool area, remove clothing, apply ice packs (groin, axilla), cool ambulance A/C, spray water and fan; monitor for shock, seizures, altered GCS; document IV fluids, neurological status, core temperature.

Additional notes include contraindications for traditional frostbite care and precautions when treating severe hypothermia or heat-related illness in the field.

nodes.title: 44. 고열
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a field-treatment flowchart appendix for Korean EMS teams.  
It gives step-by-step emergency algorithms for four critical situations:

1. Cardiac arrest / no breathing, no pulse – basic life-support sequence (ABCs, IV, oxygen, ECG, etc.).  
2. Severe hyperthermia (≥ 40 °C) – cooling measures (move to shade, ice packs, fan, mist, monitor for heat stroke/seizure).  
3. Hypoglycaemia (< 70 mg/dl) – obtain IV access, give dextrose, monitor vitals and neuro status.  
4. Poisoning / chemical exposure – scene safety, decontaminate (remove clothes, brush off powder, copious water/N-S irrigation), dress chemical burns, airway/oxygen management (including specific cautions for CO and paraquat), watch for vomiting & shock, consider antidote-capable hospital, document substance/route/amount/response.

Key reminders: protect crew & bystanders, avoid inducing emesis, do not irrigate alkali-metal or strong-acid powders, and consider HAZMAT team activation.

nodes.title: 45. 중독
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a field-treatment protocol card for Korean EMTs. It lists step-by-step actions for three main situations:  
1. General poisoning/external chemical exposure – emphasize rapid decontamination (remove powder, flush with water, strip clothes), airway/oxygen management (avoid O₂ in paraquat), shock care, and safe transport to a center that has antidotes or psychiatric services if self-harm is suspected.  
2. HAZMAT/chemical burns – note never to wash phosphorus, sodium metal, phenol, strong acids/lime; call HAZMAT team.  
3. Bites/stings (land animals, marine life) – immediate wound care, remove stingers/spines with shaving cream/powder, hot-water immersion for fish envenomation, monitor for anaphylaxis and give epinephrine IM when needed, plus mandatory documentation of exposure time, past reactions, and species involved.

nodes.title: 46. 곤충 및 해양생물에 의한 손상
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a field-first-aid protocol appendix for Korean EMS teams.  
It lists step-by-step actions after bites or stings from marine life, animals, or insects:

- Universal priorities: check ABCs & vital signs, remove stingers/spines, cleanse wound, apply ice, request medical direction.  
- Hypotension (SBP < 90): elevate legs, start IV fluid.  
- Anaphylaxis: give IM epinephrine, remove constricting items, monitor for systemic reaction.  
- Creature-specific notes: hot water for fish stings, alcohol for cnidocytes, shave cream/powder to help remove tentacles.  
- Documentation: time of injury, past reactions, photo if safe.

nodes.title: 47. 벌레 및 전갈에 의한 손상
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a field-first-aid protocol for Korean EMTs covering venomous bites/stings (bees, wasps, spiders, scorpions, snakes).  
It lists step-by-step actions: scene safety, ABCs & vitals, removal of stingers, ice packs, elevation, oxygen/ventilation support, IV access, epinephrine for anaphylaxis, limb immobilization, pressure bandage (no arterial occlusion), contraindicated measures (no incision, no cooling), required documentation (time, species, past reactions, bystander care), and phone referral to the national antivenom center.

nodes.title: 48. 뱀에 의한 손상
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a Korean-language field-triage appendix for EMS crews.  
It gives step-by-step protocols for two scenarios:

1. Suspected venomous snakebite: scene safety, ABCs, high-flow O₂, spinal-motion restriction, dry dressing & splinting, limb positioning below heart, no ice or incision, hospital antivenom check, required documentation.  
2. Violent/agitated patient: calm approach, avoid sudden moves, police-assisted restraint only (never face/neck, never prone), monitor circulation & neuro status, document need and method of restraint.

nodes.title: 49. 환자 신체 구속
nodes.summary: The excerpt is a field-treatment protocol for Korean EMTs covering four high-risk situations: (1) managing violent or agitated patients—how to approach safely, when and how to apply physical restraint (only with police present, never on face/neck, document circulation checks), and mandatory reporting items; (2) emergency care for pregnant trauma victims—left-lateral positioning, monitoring for concealed abdominal injury and eclampsia, IV/O₂, privacy, and mandatory police referral; (3) sexual-assault cases—preserve all evidence (no shower, no clothing change), use a sexual-assault kit, transport to an OB-GYN-capable hospital, protect the victim from judgment, and record injury mechanism, last meal, pain, and bleeding; and (4) general documentation requirements for each scenario.

nodes.title: 50. 성폭력 및 학대
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a field-EMS quick-reference appendix (Part 4) that summarizes critical actions for two scenarios:

1. Suspected sexual-assault / intimate-partner-violence / pregnant-trauma patients  
   - Scene & provider safety, SANE-ready hospital choice, evidence preservation, left-lateral positioning, vitals interpretation in pregnancy, mandatory reporting, forbidden behaviors (blaming, judgment), documentation points.

2. Air-medical hand-over and in-transit care for any severe trauma patient  
   - Rapid triage filters (major bleeding, airway compromise, tension pneumo, GCS < 8, shock), on-scene primary survey, life-saving interventions (bleeding control, airway, chest decompression), in-flight monitoring checklist, hospital pre-notification, repeat reassessment every 5 min, specific algorithms for head, chest and traumatic arrest.

nodes.title: 51. 항공구급 이송 중 처치
nodes.summary:
The partial document is a field-emergency-care standard guideline for Korean paramedics, focusing on aeromedical (helicopter) transport.  
Main points:  
1. Rapid in-flight assessment and treatment algorithms for life threats—massive bleeding, airway/breathing compromise, chest injury, shock, altered mental status (GCS < 8), head trauma, cardiac arrest.  
2. Mandatory pre-transport checklist: first impression, primary survey, critical interventions (bleeding control, airway opening, tension pneumothorax), spinal immobilization, IV/IO access, oxygen, monitor/AED.  
3. In-flight routine care: continuous vital-sign monitoring (BP, pulse, respiration, temp, SpO₂, EtCO₂, glucose) every 5–15 min, re-evaluation, shock positioning, warming, pain control, documentation of drugs (name-dose-time) and tubes (depth, security, patency).  
4. Special requirements for aeromedical patients: at least one IV line (two for trauma/emergencies), ECG monitoring, spinal-precaution verification, equipment securement, hypothermia check, and immediate physician contact if care deviates from algorithm.

nodes.title: 52. 이송 중 처치 및 모니터링
nodes.summary: The excerpt is a field-treatment checklist for Korean paramedics. It lists mandatory steps before and during emergency transport: spinal immobilisation for suspected trauma, minimum IV access (≥2 for critical cases, ≥1 for airlift), continuous ECG monitoring for severe/cardiac patients, and documentation of any skipped assessments. It then provides item-by-item verification boxes for drugs (correct agent, dosage, time recorded), IV lines, airway tubes (size, depth, security, patency), tourniquets (position, time, tightness), vital signs including SpO₂/ETCO₂ with reassessment, and final fixation/spine-protection checks (patient stability, hypothermia risk, belt count, equipment security).

nodes.title: 53. 이송 중 환자 관리 체크리스트

It lists mandatory steps before and during transport: spinal-motion restriction for trauma, minimum IV access (2 lines for emergencies, 1 for airlift), continuous ECG monitoring for critical patients, and documentation of drugs, tubes, tourniquets, vitals (SpO₂, ETCO₂), splints, and hypothermia risk. A second section gives the refusal-of-care algorithm: verify mental status (GCS 15), explain risks, offer physician consultation, document witness contact, and complete the refusal form if the patient still declines.

nodes.title: 54. 이송거부
nodes.summary:
The excerpt is a two-page flow-chart appendix from a Korean pre-hospital emergency-care manual.  
Page 641 gives the step-by-step protocol when a patient or guardian refuses treatment/transport: verify decision-making capacity (GCS 15 = alert/oriented), explain foreseeable consequences, offer physician phone consultation, document the refusal (patient or witness signature), and record the event.  
Page 642 presents the hospital-selection algorithm: after initial assessment, separate trauma vs. non-trauma cases, stratify severity, and route severe/multi-trauma patients to regional trauma centers, moderate cases to the nearest emergency medical center, and minor cases to local emergency facilities; if selection remains unclear after 2–3 phone checks, request direct medical direction from the dispatch center.

nodes.title: 55. 이송병원 선정 지침

Special notes cover helicopter transport for remote areas, legal/local pilot-program rules, and what to do if no accepting hospital can be found after 2–3 phone calls (call on-line medical direction / EMS dispatch center).  
A short appendix lists the same logic for specific conditions: airway obstruction, cardiac arrest, dyspnea, hyperventilation, chest pain, shock, and STEMI.

nodes.title: 56. 질환별 이송병원 선정 지침

nodes.title: 57. 소아 이송병원 선정 지침

It lists which patients (snakebite, anaphylaxis, severe poisoning, child-abuse, suicide attempt, etc.) must go to higher-level emergency facilities—regional trauma centers, regional emergency medical centers with antidotes/antivenom, or toxicology/psychiatric capability—and instructs crews to confirm hospital capacity, consider helicopter transport, and notify receiving physicians of abuse suspicions.

nodes.title: 성폭행
nodes.summary: The excerpt is a Korean-language appendix (Part 4) that outlines emergency-care protocols for elderly sexual-assault victims. It specifies referral paths: severe cases go to a regional trauma or emergency center with obstetrics/gynecology services, while less severe cases are directed to the nearest local emergency facility equipped with a sexual-violence kit. It also instructs staff to alert the receiving physician about suspected elder abuse or neglect.
